title: PRD: Private/VPC - Partition-tolerant upgrade window and operator quarantine flow
creator: Priya Raman
description: This PRD defines requirements and acceptance criteria for performing upgrades in Private/VPC deployments when one or more subnets or regions experience intermittent partitioning (partial network isolation). The goal is to provide a deterministic, auditable operator quarantine and rollback flow that preserves customer data integrity, minimizes blast radius, and supports air-gapped/offline operator environments.
goals: Define an operator quarantine mode that can be triggered automatically or manually when control-plane nodes detect partitioned worker node groups
Ensure upgrades are staged such that at least one control-plane path remains available for emergency rollback without requiring egress to Redwood-hosted mirrors
Provide clear acceptance criteria and test harness for offline/airgapped environments where image fetch may be delayed or proxied
Minimize customer-visible downtime and provide deterministic observability to support sign-off for canary progression
scope: Upgrade window orchestration across multi-subnet VPCs (single region) and operator quarantine execution
Operator behavior in 'quarantine' (no automatic image fetch, pause rollouts, preserve leader locks), with explicit human-confirmed resume
Procedures and checks for image provenance when offline mirrors are used
Telemetry and traces required for audit and on-call response during partition events
out_of_scope: Cross-region failover automation (handled by separate DR workstream)
Changes to customer-side firewall or routing topologies beyond recommended configurations
Full redesign of the operator; this PRD focuses on orchestration and process, not a rewrite
constraints: Some customers will be strictly air-gapped; any solution must support binary (physical/media) image seeding workflows
Operator must not assume continuous egress; timeouts and backoff strategies must be conservative by default
Acceptance tests must be executable in CI that simulates network partitions and mirror-lag conditions
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade orchestration exposes a 'quarantine' state that: marks affected node pools, prevents further image pulls in the isolated pools, and pauses automatic canary promotion
When quarantine is active, API surface for user workloads continues to serve existing model endpoints in read-only or degraded mode per tenancy policy
A deterministic rollback path exists that can be executed without outbound egress by using a customer-provided mirror or pre-staged artifacts
Operator produces a signed audit event for each quarantine trigger and for every manual resume or rollback action
End-to-end test suite reproduces: (a) partial subnet isolation, (b) mirror-lag (image fetch failure), and (c) operator quarantine/resume; tests must pass in CI for shipping
Runbook steps for on-call are documented and automatable (where safe) and include exact commands, expected outputs, and escalation criteria
No silent data-loss: node reinitialization in quarantine mode must not evict persistent storage without an explicit operator-led action
rollout_strategy: Phase 1 (canary): run upgrade orchestration in a non-customer-facing test harness that simulates 10% node partition scenarios
Phase 2 (pilot): enable quarantine mode opt-in for 3 pilot customers with recorded baseline telemetry
Phase 3 (gradual): default quarantine protections enabled in private deployments with a 24h monitoring window before full auto-resume is allowed
Manual override: provide a signed manual-resume API requiring two operator confirmations for air-gapped clusters
monitoring_and_tracing: New telemetry points: quarantine_trigger{reason, affected_pools, correlation_id}
Dashboards: Quarantine events timeline, affected endpoints, image-fetch failure rates, rollback latency
Tracing: end-to-end trace that correlates control-plane decisions to downstream worker kubelet states and image pull logs
decisions: Default behavior will be fail-safe: pause rollouts and surface degraded serve rather than continue risky upgrades
Automatic resume requires a quorum of control-plane health indicators across non-isolated subnets and a successful artifact checksum verification against mirror or signed bundle
Manual-resume will require signed confirmation from two on-call engineers for clusters marked as 'airgapped'
We will not rely on host-level mutable state; the operator will write ephemeral quarantine metadata to the cluster control-plane (persisted to etcd) to enable deterministic recovery
open_questions: What is the acceptable maximum delay for image fetch in 'mirror-lag' before we classify the condition as quarantine-worthy? (SRE input required)
Should we expose a customer-facing 'quarantine advisory' API to surface degraded mode to customers' own monitoring stacks?
How should we handle operator migrations where the target operator image is only available via a third-party private registry with rate limits?
